subject: Test - Retest: Modelling invariance across two phases

messages.author: 6c4d187713e325b8
messages.subject: Test - Retest: Modelling invariance across two phases
parts:
Dear all,
     I am trying to run a test-retest analysis of a two factor scale. I originally ran the model with measurementInvariance() and the analysis seemed to work well. However, since this is a test-retest analysis on the same group of people, the best bet seems to go with the longInvariance() function, which accounts for the within subject design. However, I am unable to modify the syntax to account for the scale's structure within this function. Particularly, how one alters the "varList" function to account for this model, or if the autocorr function is advisable. At the moment, the "phase" variable accounts for in which phase the data was taken, and each case number appears twice within the "casenumber"  function, once for phase one, and once for phase two (phase two is below phase one in the dataset). 

The syntax for the measurementInvariance function is below:

attach(Data)  


# Specify the Model
InvarModel <- ' Factor1 =~  item10 + item6 + item7 + item9
Factor2 =~ item13 + item8 + item4 + item5 + item18 + item12 
item6 ~~ item7'

measurementInvariance(InvarModel, data =Data, group="Phase")



Thanks for any help you can give one this,
       Conal Monaghan

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Test - Retest: Modelling invariance across two phases
parts:
The longInvariance function assumes that the same set of indicators are used at least twice. I see that you have two factors that have different lengths. I would recommend to cut the unmatched indicators and try this function again.

Sunthud

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Test - Retest: Modelling invariance across two phases
parts:
Hi Conal,

If this is the case, then your syntax included above doesn't have that information. You specified two factors measured at a single timepoint. For a two factor scale measured twice there should be 4 factors (Factor 1 Time 1, Factor 2 Time 1, Factor 1 Time 2, and Factor 2 Time 2). In addition (Sunthud can probably confirm this), I think the longInvariance function only works for a single factor measured multiple times, not multiple factors at multiple times. In your case you might have to specify the invariance models "by hand." 

Alex
